dev_probability_max_abs_diff.source: the tolerance of the coordinator's R2 replication package (1e-5 absolute, no discordant decision), used in the C1 crop check (research/c1-crop-check/README.md): there scores stored on the GPU one image at a time were reproduced within 8.9e-8 in those conditions and within 2.9e-6 on the CPU in batches of 16; here stored scores and baseline share file, CPU and batch 16; not measured before the run, since no inference precedes it; applied to the parent's scorer and to the evaluator of this script, frame by frame against the stored dev scores

dev_decisions_discordant_at_0_5.source: same R2 criterion: no decision at 0.5 may change; measured on the stored files without inference: no stored dev score of the 36 models lies within 1e-3 of 0.5 (closest 1.03e-3)

val_loss_abs.source: the absolute part of the parent runner's check (nuaa_folds_run.VAL_LOSS_TOL); its alternative 1 % branch is not used, since 1 % of the largest recorded value, 60.9868, is 0.61; measured on the stored cards without inference, the val_loss recomputed by the parent runner at run time differs from best_val_loss by at most 2.9e-6 absolute (arm_a_star_fold2_seed44, recorded 18.0934) and 2.5e-5 relative (arm_a_star_fold2_seed42, absolute 2.7e-9), two different models; the difference from val_loss_recomputed is reported, not binding

dev_accuracy_abs.source: the same number of correct dev frames (one frame = 0.0025 of 400; val_acc_at_best is the float32 of k/400); measured on the stored files without inference: the accuracy of the stored dev scores at the 0.5 decision equals val_acc_at_best for 36 of 36 models (difference 0 in float32)

softmax_of_logits_max_abs_diff.source: PROB_TOL of the parent runner (softmax of the float64 logits against the float32 probabilities); the same bound holds after the recalibration, on the dev and on the fitting, where a failure stops the run (FAIL)

consistency_rel.source: implementation check, not a baseline: the moments of the input of a layer depend only on the earlier layers, which are not changed after it, so the recomputed moments differ from the installed ones only by the float32 cast (relative 6e-8) and by the order of the float32 operations of the forward pass; 1e-4 relative is about 1,700 times the cast error and far below any change that would matter after normalisation

consistency_abs.source: absolute floor for channels whose mean or variance is zero or near zero (dead ReLU channels): 1e-6 is one thousandth of epsilon (0.001), which bounds the normalising denominator from below

stop_rule: if any baseline check fails for at least one model, the run stops before any recalibration (status BASELINE_FAILED) and the discrepancy is documented without interpretation (public/baseline.csv, per model and per check: value, reference, difference, tolerance); no re-estimated statistic is computed and nothing is read from the recalibration. An error that prevents the evaluation itself (unexpected architecture, non-finite output, SHA-256 mismatch) is a FAIL with its reason in status.json and no table

recovery_criterion.text: dev accuracy >= 0.75 and val_loss < 1.0 (val_loss from the logits); the same thresholds read on the fitting set in inference mode (accuracy and unweighted loss)
recovery_criterion.source: recovery criterion of the degenerate study (research/nuaa-degenerate-trainings/NOTE.md)

estimator.statistics: for each BatchNormalization layer, the per-channel global mean and variance of the layer INPUT over the whole fitting set of the model's arm and fold (1,400 frames for B and A*, 934 for B')
estimator.order: layer by layer in network order (bn1_1, bn1_2, bn2_1, bn2_2, bn_dense): the input of a layer is computed with the earlier layers already carrying their re-estimated statistics (one pass over the fitting set per layer)
estimator.mode: inference mode (training=False): dropout inactive, BatchNormalization layers with their moving statistics; no augmentation (frames / 255 as in scoring)
estimator.counts: values per channel: frames x H x W for the four convolutional layers (256 x 256 for bn1_1 and bn1_2, 128 x 128 for bn2_1 and bn2_2), frames for bn_dense; batches of 16, the last one shorter (1,400 = 87 x 16 + 8; 934 = 58 x 16 + 6) and weighted by its own count; the accumulated count is checked against frames x H x W
estimator.variance: population variance (divisor N) from the exact union of the batches in float64 (Chan et al.: per batch count, mean and sum of squared deviations), equal to sum of squares / N - mean^2 and to sum_b n_b (var_b + (mean_b - mean)^2) / N over the concatenated values, without the cancellation of the first form; not the mean of the batch variances, not the unweighted mean of the batch means
estimator.cast: float32, round to nearest (numpy astype) of the float64 result; the float64 values are kept in the restricted statistics file
estimator.copy: an in-memory copy (clone_model and set_weights) of the checkpoint loaded from the parent file, SHA-256 verified just before loading; the file is never opened for writing and no recalibrated .keras is saved (the copy is reproducible from the statistics file); after the five layers every weight tensor of the copy is compared byte for byte with the original: exactly the 10 moving tensors differ, each equal to the installed float32 statistic, and every other tensor (kernels, biases, gamma, beta) is bit-identical; otherwise FAIL
estimator.consistency: one multi-output pass over the fitting set with the final copy: the per-channel moments of the input of each BatchNormalization layer, recomputed with all five layers re-estimated, must equal the installed moving_mean and moving_variance within consistency_rel x |recomputed| + consistency_abs; a channel outside is an implementation failure (FAIL, no reading); the same pass gives the fitting accuracy and loss after

evaluation.input: frames / 255 in float32, assembled in key order as in the parent run
evaluation.mode: inference (training=False), checkpoint loaded with compile=False as in the parent scorer
evaluation.probability: softmax output of the layer output, column 1 (attack); in the baseline also with the parent's own scorer (nuaa_folds_run.tf_scorer on the file)
evaluation.logits: z = h @ W + b in float64 from the input of the layer output (as tf_logits of the parent runner)
evaluation.val_loss: mean categorical cross-entropy from the logits as Keras 2.15 (logsumexp(z) - z[y], no clipping: nuaa_session_ablation_run.val_loss_logits); the same unweighted formula for the fitting loss
evaluation.accuracy: argmax of the probabilities against the label (Keras CategoricalAccuracy, tie = index 0), correct / n in float32; the accuracy at the 0.5 decision is also reported
evaluation.auroc: Mann-Whitney AUROC of the attack score, attack positive, ties 0.5 (nuaa_folds_run.auroc)
evaluation.decision: attack if score_attack > 0.5, tie = bona fide (for the discordant-decision check)

batchnorm.inference: y = gamma (x - moving_mean) / sqrt(moving_variance + epsilon) + beta, per channel (Keras 2.15, training=False)
batchnorm.running_variance_in_training: recorded fact, not used: during training Keras 2.15 updated the moving variance with the Bessel-corrected batch variance for the four convolutional layers (fused kernel, factor n/(n-1), n = 16 x H x W) and with the biased batch variance for bn_dense; the population variance chosen here differs from an N/(N-1) version by the relative factor 1/(N-1): at most 1/933 for bn_dense (934 frames) and less than 1e-7 for the convolutional layers (N >= 934 x 128 x 128)

cache.linkage: y/s equal to label and subject of the manifest rows in sampling order (spread per class)

folds_run.public_files: not opened (its aggregate holds test metrics)

sources.rule: every manifest row found exactly once, in the cache or in the extracted frames file

parent_run.aggregate_json: read as bytes and compared with its SHA256SUMS line; never parsed (it holds test metrics)
parent_run.keys: fitting_keys_sha256 and dev_keys_sha256 of every card equal to the manifests

checks.test: the fold schema (fold<k>_test.csv, the test role of our folds) is never opened and no <model>_test_scores.csv is opened; the M2 manifests official_test and cnn_test (NUAA's official image lists, not the test role of our folds) are read only to index the cache; as in the parent run the frame files (cache and extracted frames) are hashed and loaded whole, but only fitting and dev frames are assembled; the public aggregate of the parent run, which holds test metrics, is read only as bytes for its SHA-256 and never parsed; no public file of the folds run is opened; no test frame is assembled or evaluated and no test score or metric is read, computed or written
